title: Work
about: Collocations for talking about work: jobs and careers, the language of job adverts, and everyday tasks at work, such as a demanding job, climb the career ladder, fill a vacancy and hand in your notice.

parts.title: Things you might do at work

items.pattern: adjective + noun · a fulfilling / rewarding / satisfying job · find your job fulfilling
items.meaning: a job that makes you feel happy and useful because you are doing something worthwhile
items.uk: робота, що приносить задоволення й відчуття сенсу
items.example: Teaching small children is tiring, but it's a really **fulfilling job**.
more: After twenty years in an office, he found a **rewarding job** at an animal shelter.
I want a **fulfilling job**, not just one that pays the bills.
items.watchOut: Не a satisfied job: satisfied (задоволений) — про людину: I'm satisfied with my job. Про саму роботу — fulfilling, rewarding або satisfying. Rewarding — про моральну винагороду, а не про гроші; прибуткова робота — a well-paid або lucrative job.

items.pattern: adjective + noun · a high-powered job / lawyer / businesswoman
items.meaning: an important job with a lot of responsibility and influence
items.example: My aunt has a **high-powered job** in a law firm, so she's always on the phone.
more: He gave up his **high-powered job** in the city to open a small café by the sea.
Her parents both have **high-powered jobs**, so the children see a lot of their grandmother.
items.watchOut: High-powered — про важливість і відповідальність посади, а не про силу. Це не обов'язково «високооплачувана»: високооплачувана робота — a well-paid job.

items.pattern: adjective + noun · a demanding job / role / boss · physically / mentally demanding
items.meaning: a job that needs a lot of your time, energy and effort
items.uk: важка, виснажлива робота (що забирає багато сил і часу)
items.example: Being a paramedic is a **demanding job**, both physically and emotionally.
more: With a **demanding job** and two small children, she hardly has time to read.
He wanted a less **demanding job** so he could spend more evenings with his family.
items.watchOut: Не a requiring job і не a hard-working job: hard-working (працьовитий) — про людину. Demanding — про роботу, що забирає багато сил; про людину — вимогливий: a demanding boss.

items.pattern: adjective + noun · a steady / permanent / secure job · opposite: a temporary job
items.meaning: a regular job that is likely to continue for a long time, so you can count on the money
items.example: My brother has finally found a **steady job** at the post office, so he can start saving.
more: They want to buy a flat, but first she needs a **permanent job**.
Without a **steady job**, it's hard to get a loan from the bank.
items.watchOut: «Постійна робота» — a permanent / steady job, а не a constant job: constant — «безперервний, що не припиняється» (constant noise). Протилежне — a temporary job.

items.pattern: verb + for + noun · apply for a job / a post / a position · apply to a company · a job application
items.meaning: formally ask to be given a job, usually by sending a form or your CV
items.uk: подаватися на вакансію, надсилати заявку (резюме) на роботу
items.example: I've **applied for a job** at the new garden centre. Fingers crossed!
more: She **applied for** twenty **jobs** before she got an interview.
If you want to **apply for the job**, send your CV by Friday.
items.watchOut: Прийменник — for: apply for a job / a post. Apply to — до організації: apply to a hospital, apply to a university. Не submit for a job.

items.pattern: verb + sb + noun · offer sb a job · offer a job to sb · be offered a job · accept / turn down a job offer
items.meaning: say that you want someone to work for you
items.example: The hotel manager liked Anna so much that he **offered her a job** on the spot.
more: I've **been offered a job** in Manchester, but I'm not sure I want to move.
They **offered the job to** someone with more experience.
items.watchOut: «Запропонувати роботу» — offer sb a job, а не propose a job: propose — запропонувати ідею чи план або освідчитися. «Мені запропонували роботу» — I was offered a job: людина стає підметом.

items.pattern: verb + particle + noun · carry out work / repairs / tests · work is carried out
items.meaning: do a piece of work, such as building, repairing or checking something
items.example: Builders are **carrying out work** on the bridge, so the road is closed.
more: The landlord promised to **carry out the work** on our roof before winter.
**Work** on the school hall **was carried out** during the summer holidays.
items.watchOut: «Проводити роботи» — carry out work, а не hold works. Work тут зазвичай незлічуване: some work, a lot of work, без a. Множину works у Британії вживають про будівельні чи ремонтні роботи: roadworks (ремонт дороги), building works, The works will finish in May.

items.pattern: verb + noun · supervise work / staff / a project · a supervisor
items.meaning: watch work while it is being done to make sure it is done properly
items.example: Our foreman **supervises the work** of twelve builders.
more: A senior nurse **supervises the work** of the students on the ward.
Dad stood in the garden all afternoon, **supervising** my brother's **work** on the new fence.
items.watchOut: «Контролювати роботу» в значенні «перевіряти, наглядати» — supervise або oversee work. Control означає «керувати, тримати під контролем» (control a car, control your temper), тому в значенні «перевіряти» не підходить.

items.pattern: verb + noun · complete the work / a task / a course · the work is completed
items.meaning: finish all of a piece of work
items.example: The painters **completed the work** two days early, so we could move in sooner.
more: She stayed late to **complete her work** before the holidays.
The **work** on the new playground **was completed** in just three weeks.
items.watchOut: Complete — трохи офіційніше, ніж finish. Не end the work: end кажуть про подію, що закінчується (the meeting ended).

items.pattern: verb + adverb + with · work closely with sb · work closely together
items.meaning: work together with someone a lot, sharing information and helping each other
items.example: Teachers **work closely with** parents to help children who are struggling.
more: In the kitchen, the chef **works closely with** the two cooks every evening.
As a social worker, she **works closely with** doctors and the police.
items.watchOut: «Тісно співпрацювати» — work closely with (прислівник closely), а не work narrowly / nearly. Work close to sth — працювати неподалік: I work close to the station.

items.pattern: verb + particle + noun · take on (extra / too much) work · take on staff
items.meaning: agree to do some work or to be responsible for it
items.uk: братися за роботу, брати на себе (додаткову) роботу
items.example: Since my colleague left, I've had to **take on** some of his **work**.
more: Don't **take on** any more **work** until you've finished what you've got.
Our builder has **taken on** too much **work**, so our job keeps getting delayed.
items.watchOut: Take on work — погодитися виконати, взяти на себе. Take on staff — найняти працівників. Take over — повністю перебрати чужу справу: take over the shop.

items.pattern: be + adjective + to-infinitive · be available to start work (immediately / at short notice / in June)
items.meaning: be free and ready to begin a new job
items.uk: мати змогу (бути готовим) приступити до роботи
items.example: The interviewer asked me when I'd be **available to start work**.
more: She's leaving her old job in May, so she'll be **available to start work** in June.
Students who are **available to start work** in July get the best summer jobs.
items.watchOut: Available — «вільний, може приступити», звичне слово в оголошеннях і на співбесідах: When are you available to start? Start work — без артикля: I start work at eight.

items.pattern: verb + noun · wreck / ruin / destroy sb's career · a scandal / an injury ruins a career
items.meaning: damage someone's career so badly that it cannot continue
items.example: A bad knee injury **ruined his career** as a footballer at twenty-three.
more: One angry interview nearly **wrecked her career**.
He was afraid the mistake would **ruin his career**, but his boss forgave him.
items.watchOut: «Зламати кар'єру» — ruin / wreck sb's career, а не break sb's career. Spoil — зіпсувати щось менше: spoil the evening, spoil the view.

items.pattern: verb + on + noun · embark on a career (in sth / as sth) · formal; in conversation: start a career
items.meaning: start a new career
items.example: At fifty, my aunt **embarked on a new career** as a driving instructor.
more: After university, he **embarked on a career** in nursing.
Many young people **embark on a career** without knowing what they really want.
items.watchOut: Embark on — книжне, буквально «сісти на корабель». Прийменник — on. У розмові частіше кажуть start a career.

items.phrase: at the height / peak of your career
items.pattern: at + the + noun + of · at the height / peak of your career / fame
items.meaning: at the time when you are most successful in your career
items.example: She retired from tennis **at the peak of her career**, aged only twenty-nine.
more: **At the height of her career**, the model's face was on every magazine cover.
Many sportspeople find it hard to accept that the **peak of their career** is behind them.
items.watchOut: «На піку кар'єри» — at the peak / height of your career, з прийменником at (не on і не in). Peak /piːk/ — довге «і»; не плутай з pick (вибирати).

items.pattern: verb + noun + in · have / want a career in medicine / teaching / the law · a career as a doctor
items.meaning: work in a particular profession for many years
items.uk: працювати в галузі (медицини), будувати кар'єру в (медицині)
items.example: My cousin wants to **have a career in** medicine, like her mum.
more: He **had a long career in** teaching before he retired.
If you want **a career in** hotel management, start by working on reception.
items.watchOut: Галузь — in: a career in medicine, a career in the law. Професія — as: a career as a doctor. Не a career of medicine. Вимова: /kəˈrɪə/, наголос на другому складі; не плутай з carrier /ˈkæriə/ (перевізник).

items.pattern: noun + verb · sb's career lasted / spanned forty years · a career spanning forty years
items.meaning: someone's career went on for a particular, usually long, time
items.example: My grandfather was a postman, and his **career lasted** forty-two years.
more: The footballer's **career spanned** three countries and twenty years.
Her **career** on television **lasted** longer than anyone expected.
items.watchOut: «Кар'єра тривала сорок років» — lasted forty years, а не continued forty years: continue — продовжуватися далі. Span — книжне «охоплювати (період)»: a career spanning forty years.

items.pattern: adjective + noun · a brilliant / glittering / distinguished career
items.meaning: a very successful career that people admire
items.example: After a **brilliant career** as a surgeon, she now teaches young doctors.
more: Everyone at school expected him to have a **glittering career**, but he chose to become a farmer.
The newspaper wrote about her **brilliant career** in fashion.
items.watchOut: «Блискуча кар'єра» — a brilliant або glittering career. Не shiny career: shiny — блискучий про поверхню (shiny shoes).

items.pattern: verb + noun · climb / move up the career ladder · get onto the career ladder
items.meaning: move to better and more important jobs, step by step
items.example: He started as a waiter and slowly **climbed the career ladder** to hotel manager.
more: She wasn't interested in **climbing the career ladder**. She just liked her job.
It's hard to **climb the career ladder** when you work part-time.
items.watchOut: «Кар'єрні сходи» — the career ladder (буквально драбина), а не career stairs. Зазвичай з дієсловом climb або move up.

items.pattern: adjective + noun · a promising career / start / young player · opposite: a dead-end job
items.meaning: a career that looks likely to be successful in the future
items.example: She gave up a **promising career** in law to look after her sick father.
more: A car accident ended his **promising career** as a racing cyclist.
After winning a national competition, the young pianist had a **promising career** ahead of her.
items.watchOut: «Перспективна кар'єра» — a promising career, а не a perspective career: perspective — точка зору, погляд. Протилежне — a dead-end job: робота без жодних перспектив.

items.pattern: noun + verb · sb's career takes off · also: a business / sales take off
items.meaning: a career suddenly becomes very successful
items.example: His **career took off** when a famous chef tasted his cakes at a village fair.
more: The band played in pubs for years before their **career** finally **took off**.
Her **career took off** after a famous magazine put her photos on the cover.
items.watchOut: Take off — і «злітати» про літак, і «раптом стати успішним». «Кар'єра пішла вгору» — her career took off, не went up. Додатка тут немає.

items.pattern: adjective + noun + of · have a good / detailed / basic knowledge of sth
items.meaning: know a lot about a subject
items.uk: добре знати щось, добре розумітися на чомусь
items.example: Our tour guide had a **good knowledge of** local history.
more: To work in a garden centre, you need a **good knowledge of** plants.
She has a **good knowledge of** French and German, so she works on reception.
items.watchOut: Тут кажуть a good knowledge of (з a), хоча knowledge незлічуване: не good knowledges. Прийменник — of: a good knowledge of cooking. Вимова: /ˈnɒlɪdʒ/, k не читається.

items.pattern: verb + noun + in / of · have experience in sales · have experience of working with children · five years' experience
items.meaning: have done a type of work before, so you know how to do it
items.example: Do you **have** any **experience in** customer service?
more: We're looking for someone who **has experience of** working with young children.
She **has** ten years' **experience in** catering.
items.watchOut: Досвід роботи — experience, незлічуване: a lot of experience, не experiences. An experience — подія, враження: a strange experience. Галузь — in (experience in sales), дія — of + -ing (experience of working with children).

items.pattern: adjective + noun + noun · be a good team player
items.meaning: a person who works well with other people in a group
items.uk: людина, яка вміє працювати в команді; командний гравець
items.example: Lisa's not the fastest nurse on the ward, but she's a **good team player**.
more: The manager said I was a **good team player** because I always help my colleagues.
We need a **good team player**, not someone who wants all the credit.
items.watchOut: Команда людей — team, а не command: command — наказ. A good team player — ідіома не лише про спорт: людина, яка вміє працювати з іншими.

items.pattern: adjective + noun · a stimulating / friendly / pleasant working (or work) environment
items.meaning: a place of work where people and tasks keep you interested and help you learn
items.uk: цікаве робоче середовище, що надихає й розвиває
items.example: The school offers a **stimulating working environment** and plenty of training.
more: She left the bank because she wanted a more **stimulating working environment**.
A **stimulating working environment** is more important to me than a big salary.
items.watchOut: Stimulating тут — «цікавий, такий, що змушує думати й розвиватися», а не «стимулювальний» про ліки чи каву. Робоче середовище — working environment (або work environment).

items.pattern: adjective + noun + of · be an integral part of a team / sb's life
items.meaning: a necessary and important part, which the whole can't do without
items.example: Our cleaners are an **integral part** of the hospital team.
more: Music has always been an **integral part** of our family life.
Visiting museums is an **integral part** of the school trip.
items.watchOut: «Невід'ємна частина» — an integral part (або an essential part). Вимова: /ˈɪntɪɡrəl/, наголос на першому складі, не «інтеґрáл».

items.pattern: adjective + noun · a close / close-knit team
items.meaning: a group of people who work well together and get on well
items.example: There are only six of us in the office, and we're a **close team**.
more: The nurses on the night shift are a **close team** who look after each other.
It's easier to start a new job when you join a **close team**.
items.watchOut: Close тут — прикметник «близький, згуртований», вимова /kləʊs/ (як у close friend), а не /kləʊz/ (зачиняти). Не closed team: closed — зачинений. Ще кажуть a close-knit team.

items.pattern: noun + noun · get job satisfaction · high / low job satisfaction
items.meaning: the good feeling you get from doing your job
items.example: For most nurses, **job satisfaction** matters more than money.
more: I get a lot of **job satisfaction** from seeing my pupils improve.
Long hours and rude customers mean **job satisfaction** at the shop is very low.
items.watchOut: Усталений вираз — job satisfaction (іменник + іменник). Можна сказати get satisfaction from your work, але не job pleasure чи work pleasure.

items.pattern: adjective + noun · offer generous benefits · a benefits package
items.meaning: good rewards for work besides the salary, such as a company car, a pension or long holidays
items.uk: щедрий соцпакет, хороші пільги від роботодавця
items.example: The supermarket pays an average wage but offers **generous benefits**, like free meals and staff discounts.
more: The job comes with **generous benefits**, including private health insurance.
Teachers here don't earn much, but the **benefits** are **generous**: long holidays and a good pension.
items.watchOut: «Соцпакет» — benefits або a benefits package, а не social package. Обережно: у Британії be on benefits — жити на державну допомогу.

items.pattern: verb + noun · fill a vacancy / post / position · the vacancy is filled · there's a vacancy for sth
items.meaning: find someone to do a job that is free, and they accept it
items.example: The café needs to **fill the vacancy** before the summer season starts.
more: We had over a hundred applications, and **the vacancy was filled** within a week.
The hospital is struggling to **fill vacancies** for porters.
items.watchOut: «Закрити вакансію», тобто знайти людину, — fill a vacancy. The vacancy is closed означає інше: заявки більше не приймають. Вимова: /ˈveɪkənsi/; vacation (відпустка, канікули) — інше слово.

items.pattern: verb + noun + as · have / get a job as a nurse · work as a nurse
items.meaning: work in a particular job
items.example: My sister **has a job as** a receptionist at the dentist's.
more: He **had a job as** a lifeguard every summer when he was a student.
She'd like to **get a job as** a teaching assistant.
items.watchOut: Кажуть have a job, а не have a work: work у значенні «робота» незлічуване (I have a lot of work). Після as потрібен артикль: a job as a nurse, не as nurse.

items.pattern: verb + noun + of · take charge of sth / sb · be in charge of sth
items.meaning: become responsible for something or someone and control it
items.example: When the head chef is ill, Tom **takes charge of** the kitchen.
more: The new manager will **take charge of** the shop in April.
Grandma **took charge of** the wedding preparations, and everything went perfectly.
items.watchOut: Без артикля: take charge of, не take the charge of. Be in charge of — уже відповідати за щось (стан), take charge of — взяти це на себе (дія).

items.pattern: verb + adjective · sth goes wrong · something / nothing / everything went wrong
items.meaning: stop working properly, or not happen the way you planned
items.example: Everything **went wrong** on my first day: I got lost and was an hour late.
more: If anything **goes wrong** while I'm away, call me.
The dishwasher **went wrong** again, so we washed everything by hand.
items.watchOut: «Щось пішло не так» — something went wrong, а не went not so і не went bad: go bad — зіпсуватися про їжу (the milk went bad).

items.pattern: verb + noun · make / book an appointment (with sb / for Monday) · have an appointment
items.meaning: arrange a time to see someone such as a doctor, a hairdresser or a client
items.uk: записатися на прийом; домовитися про зустріч
items.example: Mum **made an appointment** at the eye clinic for next Tuesday.
more: Could you **make an appointment** for me to see the bank manager?
You can **make an appointment** at the hairdresser's online.
items.watchOut: «Записатися до лікаря» — make (або book) an appointment, а не write myself to the doctor: це калька з «записатися». Appointment — домовлена зустріч, прийом; побачення — a date.

items.pattern: verb + noun · keep an appointment · opposite: miss / cancel an appointment
items.meaning: go to an appointment you arranged, at the agreed time
items.example: A good salesman **keeps his appointments** and never makes clients wait.
more: Patients who don't **keep their appointments** cost the hospital a lot of money.
My son is eighteen now, so he has to remember to **keep** his own **appointments**.
items.watchOut: Keep an appointment — прийти, як домовлялися, а не «тримати» чи «зберігати». Протилежне — miss an appointment (пропустити). Не visit an appointment.

items.pattern: verb + noun · answer the phone / a call · pick up the phone
items.meaning: pick up the phone when it rings and speak to the caller
items.example: Can you **answer the phone**? My hands are covered in flour.
more: Nobody **answered the phone** at the doctor's, so I went there in person.
Her job is mostly **answering the phone** and dealing with customers' questions.
items.watchOut: «Взяти слухавку» — answer the phone або pick up (the phone), а не take the phone (take — просто взяти телефон у руки). Без прийменника: answer the phone, не answer to the phone.

items.pattern: verb + noun · field (telephone) calls / questions · field calls for sb
items.meaning: deal with phone calls yourself so that another person only gets the most important ones
items.example: In the busy season, the hotel manager's assistant **fields** most of his **calls**.
more: The school secretary **fielded calls** from worried parents all morning.
After the match, the coach had to **field** a lot of difficult **questions** from journalists.
items.watchOut: Field тут — дієслово «приймати й розбиратися» (з крикету: ловити м'яч на полі). Це більше, ніж answer: людина сама вирішує, що робити з дзвінком, і з'єднує лише з найважливішими.

items.pattern: verb + noun · make a reservation (for two / for Friday) · book a table / a room
items.meaning: arrange for a table, room or seat to be kept for you
items.example: I've **made a reservation** for six at the Italian restaurant.
more: Could you **make a reservation** for me at a hotel near the station?
You don't need to **make a reservation**: it's a small café.
items.watchOut: «Забронювати» — make a reservation або просто book (book a table / a room), а не do a reservation.

items.pattern: verb + noun · give / do / make a presentation (to sb / on sth)
items.meaning: talk to a group of people about a subject, often with slides
items.example: Our new manager **gave a presentation** about the company's plans for next year.
more: Each pupil **gave a short presentation** on their favourite animal.
She was nervous before she **gave the presentation**, but it went well.
items.watchOut: «Робити презентацію» — give a presentation (у розмові ще do або make), а не tell або speak a presentation. Про сам виступ кажуть give, не hold.

items.pattern: verb + noun · make (all the) preparations for sth
items.meaning: do the things you need to do so that you are ready for an event
items.uk: готуватися (до події), робити все потрібне заздалегідь
items.example: My parents are **making preparations** for their fortieth wedding anniversary.
more: The school is **making** all the **preparations** for the summer fair.
Have you **made** any **preparations** for the trip yet?
items.watchOut: «Готуватися до чогось» — make preparations for sth (preparations у множині); з do так зазвичай не кажуть. Те саме дієсловом — prepare for sth.

items.pattern: verb + noun · make / take a photocopy (of sth) · make copies · photocopy sth
items.meaning: copy documents on a photocopier
items.example: Can you **make** ten **photocopies** of this letter before the meeting?
more: The machine in the post office lets you **make photocopies** for 10p a page.
Don't forget to **make a photocopy** of your passport before you travel.
items.watchOut: Копія — a photocopy, апарат — a photocopier (не xerox: це назва фірми, і в Британії так майже не кажуть). Дієслово — make (або take) a photocopy; do some photocopying — займатися ксерокопіюванням.

items.pattern: verb + noun · arrange / set up / organise a meeting (with sb / for Monday)
items.meaning: plan a meeting and agree when and where it will be
items.example: I'll **arrange a meeting** with the builders to talk about the price.
more: The head teacher **arranged a meeting** with all the parents.
Can we **arrange a meeting** for Monday to talk about the new rota?
items.watchOut: «Призначити зустріч» — arrange (або set up, organise) a meeting, а не appoint a meeting: appoint — призначити людину на посаду.

items.pattern: verb + noun · take the minutes (at / of a meeting) · the minutes of the last meeting
items.meaning: write the official notes of what is said and decided at a meeting
items.example: At every staff meeting, one person **takes the minutes** and sends them to everyone.
more: At our residents' association, my neighbour always **takes the minutes**.
I hate **taking the minutes**: I can't listen and write at the same time.
items.watchOut: Minutes тут — не хвилини, а протокол зборів (завжди у множині): take the minutes. «Вести протокол» — не write the protocol: protocol — це правила, етикет.

items.pattern: verb + noun + of · keep a record / records of sth
items.meaning: regularly write down information about something so you can check it later
items.example: I **keep a record** of all the money I spend on the car.
more: Nurses **keep a record** of every medicine they give.
**Keep a record** of the hours you work, so you get paid for all of them.
items.watchOut: «Вести облік (записи)» — keep a record, а не lead a record. Наголос: іменник record — /ˈrekɔːd/, дієслово record — /rɪˈkɔːd/.

items.pattern: verb + noun · set (yourself / sb) a target / targets / goals · meet / reach a target
items.meaning: decide what you or other people should achieve, often by a certain time
items.example: Our manager **sets** us monthly sales **targets**.
more: Good teachers **set** their pupils **targets** that are hard but possible.
Don't **set** your **targets** too high or you'll feel like a failure.
items.watchOut: «Ставити цілі» — set targets / goals, а не put targets: put — фізично покласти. Виконати план — meet / reach / hit a target.

items.pattern: verb + noun · achieve / reach your goal(s) · achieve a target / an aim
items.meaning: succeed in doing what you planned to do
items.example: With hard work, she **achieved her goal** of becoming a head teacher by forty.
more: Write down your **goals**: it makes it easier to **achieve** them.
Few people **achieve** all their **goals** in life, and that's OK.
items.watchOut: «Досягти мети» — achieve / reach a goal, без прийменника (не achieve to a goal). Goal у футболі — гол, і там кажуть score a goal.

items.pattern: verb + noun · make / write a list (of sth) · a shopping / to-do list
items.meaning: write down a series of things you need to do, buy or remember
items.example: Before I go to the supermarket, I always **make a list**.
more: She **made a list** of everyone she wanted to invite to the party.
If you've got lots to do, **make a list** and start with the hardest job.
items.watchOut: «Скласти список» — make (або write) a list, а не fold a list: fold — складати папір чи одяг. Список справ — a to-do list.

items.pattern: verb + particle + noun · hand in / give in your notice · resign
items.meaning: formally tell your employer that you are going to leave your job
items.uk: подати заяву про звільнення (за власним бажанням)
items.example: She **handed in her notice** because she'd found a better job closer to home.
more: If you want to leave, you have to **hand in your notice** a month before.
He was so angry with his boss that he **handed in his notice** the same day.
items.watchOut: «Звільнитися за власним бажанням» — hand in your notice або resign, а не write a statement (калька з «написати заяву»). Notice тут — офіційне попередження про звільнення.

items.pattern: verb + adjective + noun · take early retirement · retire early
items.meaning: stop working before the usual age for leaving work
items.example: Dad **took early retirement** at fifty-eight to spend more time in his garden.
more: Because of his bad back, he had to **take early retirement**.
Many teachers would love to **take early retirement**, but they can't afford it.
items.watchOut: «Вийти на пенсію» — retire або take retirement, а не go on pension. Pension — це гроші, пенсійна виплата: get a pension.

warmup.uk: У неї хороша робота в банку.
warmup.q: She has a good ___ at the bank.
warmup.explain: Мати роботу — have a job. Work у цьому значенні незлічуване, тому не a work.
Постійна робота — a permanent або steady job. Constant — безперервний (constant noise).
Кар'єрні сходи — the career ladder, буквально «драбина».

warmup.uk: Я записався до лікаря на п'ятницю.
warmup.q: I've ___ an appointment with the doctor for Friday.
warmup.explain: Записатися на прийом — make (або book) an appointment.
Вести протокол — take the minutes. Protocol — це правила, етикет.

warmup.uk: Учора вона подала заяву про звільнення.
warmup.explain: Звільнитися за власним бажанням — hand in your notice.
Вийти на пенсію — retire або take retirement. Pension — пенсія як гроші.
Соцпакет — benefits (a benefits package). Social package і preferences — кальки, так не кажуть.

A.q: Her career ___ off when her first song went to number one.
A.explain: Кар'єра пішла вгору — her career took off, як літак, що злітає.

A.q: Mum was happy when I got a ___ job with a pension and paid holidays.
A.explain: Постійна робота — a permanent або steady job. Constant — безперервний.

A.q: They ___ me the job, but I said no because the pay was too low.
A.explain: Запропонувати роботу — offer sb a job. Propose — запропонувати ідею чи план або освідчитися.

B.q: Is he a good ___ player? In this job he'll work with ten other nurses.
B.explain: Людина, яка добре працює з іншими, — a good team player. Command — наказ, а не команда людей.

B.q: Generous ___ are one reason why people stay at the company for years.
Fixing old bikes and seeing kids ride them again gives Sam real job ___.
B.explain: Задоволення від роботи — job satisfaction, усталений вираз.

C.q: I can't come to the meeting on Friday. Could you take the ___ for me?
C.explain: Вести протокол — take the minutes. Protocol — це правила, етикет.

C.q: The parents asked the school to ___ a meeting about the new bus timetable.
C.explain: Домовитися про зустріч — arrange a meeting. Appoint — призначити людину на посаду.

C.q: Did you remember to ___ a reservation at the hotel?
C.explain: Забронювати — make a reservation або просто book a table.

example.title: Time for a change
example.uk:
Дванадцять років Марта працювала менеджеркою у великому супермаркеті. Робота була виснажлива: вона ставила плани сорока працівникам, вела облік кожної поставки й писала протоколи нескінченних нарад. Платили добре, але задоволення від роботи не було.

Одного вечора вона побачила оголошення: маленькій ветеринарній клініці потрібна була адміністраторка, яка могла б приступити до роботи в червні. Того ж вечора вона подалася на цю вакансію, а за тиждень їй запропонували роботу.

Наступного ранку вона подала заяву про звільнення. Начальник був приголомшений. «Ти ж кидаєш перспективну кар'єру!» — сказав він. Але Марта лише всміхнулася. Тепер вона працює в дружній команді ветеринарів і медсестер, і ще жодна робота не давала їй стільки радості й відчуття сенсу.
example.en:
For twelve years, Marta [[had a job as|c1]] a manager in a big supermarket. It was a [[demanding job|a3]]: she [[set targets|c15]] for forty staff, [[kept a record|c14]] of every delivery and [[took the minutes|c13]] at endless meetings. The pay was good, but there was no [[job satisfaction|b7]].

One evening she saw an advert: a small animal hospital needed a receptionist who was [[available to start work|a12]] in June. She [[applied for the job|a5]] that night, and a week later they [[offered her the job|a6]].

The next morning she [[handed in her notice|c18]]. Her boss was shocked. 'You're throwing away a [[promising career|a20]]!' he said. But Marta just smiled. Now she works in a [[close team|b6]] of vets and nurses, and it's the most [[fulfilling job|a1]] she's ever had.
